Topic: The Magic of Dandelin Spheres: Visualizing Conic Sections

Target audience: High school geometry students or early undergraduates

Section: section_1 — Prerequisites: The Cone and the Plane

Lecture lines:
Conic sections result from plane-cone intersections.
Imagine a flashlight creating shapes on a wall.
The intersection angle determines the specific shape.

Planned animations:
Fade in a wireframe double-napped cone in #FFFFFF.
Fade in a transparent cutting plane intersecting the cone at an angle.
Highlight the resulting ellipse intersection curve in #FF00FF.

Section: section_2 — Introducing Dandelin Spheres

Lecture lines:
Place a sphere inside the cone.
Make it tangent to the cone surface.
Make it tangent to the cutting plane.
This is a Dandelin sphere.
It reveals hidden geometry inside.

Planned animations:
Fade in two spheres inside the cone, tangent to the inner walls.
Translate the cutting plane until it touches both spheres.
Add small points of color #00FFFF at the exact contact points on the plane.

Section: section_3 — The Geometry of Proof (Focus: Ellipse)

Lecture lines:
Ellipse has two Dandelin spheres.
Each touches the plane at a focus.
Points on the ellipse follow distance rules.
Distances to foci sum to a constant.
This defines the ellipse perfectly.

Planned animations:
Draw a point P moving slowly along the ellipse perimeter.
Draw two line segments from P to the contact point foci.
Display the sum of lengths as a text label near P in #FFFF00.
Maintain the length sum constant as P orbits the ellipse.
Flash the foci in #00FFFF to emphasize their role.

Section: section_4 — Expanding to Parabola and Hyperbola

Lecture lines:
Change the plane angle to shift shapes.
Parabolas use one sphere tangent to plane.
Hyperbolas require spheres in both cones.

Planned animations:
Adjust the cutting plane angle until parallel to a slant edge of the cone.
Remove one sphere, keeping only the sphere tangent to the new parabolic cut.
Rotate the cone to reveal the hyperbola, adding a second sphere in the opposite nappe.

Section: section_5 — Summary and Synthesis

Lecture lines:
Dandelin spheres connect 3D and 2D.
They explain conic properties geometrically.
Now you visualize conic sections clearly.

Planned animations:
Rotate the whole setup to provide a clear 3D perspective.
Animate the cutting plane smoothly cycling through all conic angles.
Sync the spheres to shrink or grow while maintaining tangency.

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject
